moat_against: Pure commodity price-taker: roic_proxy -40%/-47% in 2019/2020 vs +70% in 2022 — the cycle, not the company, sets returns
Depleting asset base: reserves must be continuously replaced with capex (FY2025 additions to oil and gas property $2,740M vs OCF $4,545M)
Egypt concentration under production-sharing contracts: higher oil prices mechanically reduce APA's adjusted (entitlement) volumes; sovereign/arrears risk
Share count rose with the all-stock Callon acquisition (diluted 309M in FY2023 to 359M in FY2025) — per-share compounding diluted by M&A
Gas price weakness: Q2 2026 realized U.S. gas price collapsed year over year, offsetting oil strength
moat_for: Permian capital efficiency: U.S. oil guidance raised to 123,000 bbl/d at unchanged $1.3B U.S. capital; 4 rigs sustaining output once estimated to need 8
GranMorgu (Suriname Block 58) carried economics: TotalEnergies funds 87.5% of the first $10B gross development capex; first oil targeted mid-2028
Egypt gas re-pricing: nearly half of Egyptian gas production now under a revised, higher-price agreement
Cost program: exit-2026 annualized run-rate savings target raised to $500M; LOE guidance cut
moat_justification: Commodity price-taker with no pricing power: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json swings from -40.3% (2019) and -47.2% (2020) to +70.4% (2022), +37.6% (2023), +16.6% (2024) and +18.6% (2025) — returns are set by oil and gas prices, not by a franchise. Gross margin is not filed under any engine-read tag (revenue itself is filed only under a filer extension concept), so no margin evidence offsets that. What APA does have is asset quality, not a moat: Permian drilling/completion efficiency gains (full-year U.S. oil guidance raised to 123,000 bbl/d on an unchanged $1.3B U.S. capital budget, four rigs doing the work once estimated to need eight), a revised Egypt gas pricing agreement covering nearly half its Egyptian gas, and the carried GranMorgu development in Suriname (TotalEnergies pays 87.5% of the first $10B of gross capex). Those support a 3, not the 7+ the rubric reserves for durable above-cost-of-capital returns through a cycle — APA's own history includes two deeply negative ROIC years in the last seven.
name: APA Corporation
one_liner: Commodity E&P, moat 3/10 — no pricing power and cycle-set returns; on the override-free TTM base ($5.67/share, filed E&P capex now read by engine 5.5) the weighted IRR is 12.45% with IV@15% $39.16 vs the $49.14 price, so it does not clear the 15% hurdle (clears only below ~$39.16); band D (8.57%) to B (17.14%) — size to the bear end.

sbc_override.source: Last filed SBC: FY2025 AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $107,000,000 (Form 10-K FY2025, filed 2026-02-26) — the anchor named here; value is exactly 1.0x that filed figure, inside the 0.1x-10x estimate band
sbc_override.reason: APA tags SBC only in annual filings; its 10-Q cash-flow statements present no stock-compensation adjustment line at all (verified in the Q2 2026 10-Q, accession 0001841666-26-000053: the operating-activities reconciliation lists DD&A, deferred taxes, dry-hole and other items, with no SBC line), so ttm.py exits with 'sbc: no post-FY YTD fact' and no TTM base can be built. This override lets ttm.py assemble the SBC legs at the last filed annual rate, prorated by days. SBC is ~2.4% of FY2025 OCF ($107M vs $4,545M), so the proration assumption moves TTM OE/share by cents, not dollars. The engine's annual history is unaffected: SBC is filed for every annual period, and an override never replaces a filed value.
